To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chemokine receptors can signal in a biased manner and that biased signaling can be regulated by ligand and receptor polymorphisms.
the CCR7 ligand, CCL21, is a more potent agonist than CCL19, and that biased signaling of the CCR7 receptor can be regulated at the level of the ligand, the receptor, or the signaling pathway.

CCR7 signaling can be biased by CCL19 or CCL21, that CCR7 is regulated by multiple layers of regulation at multiple intersections, and that the CCR7 axis has a major impact on the development and maintenance of the adaptive immune system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanisms of biased signaling of the chemokines CCL19 and 21 and their receptor CCR7 in leukocytes.
the molecular basis of biased CCR7 signaling.
the elucidation of the mechanisms that regulate CCR7 function in order to gain insight into the pathobiology of CCR7 mediated processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CCR7 system has been designed to be highly flexible, allowing the immune system to respond in a rapid and specific way to different stimuli.
CCL19 and/or CCL21 are not redundant, but rather that CCR7 signaling is biased by the ligands CCL21 and CCL19.
CCR7 and CCL19/C21 have a very complex signaling network and that the regulation of this signaling network is very complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CCR7 chemokine receptor is an excellent paradigm for biased signaling, which is a key concept in G protein coupled receptor biology.

biased signaling of the CCR7 chemokine receptors is an important mechanism of chemokine receptor regulation and that biased signaling of CCR7 by CCL21 and CCL19 can have differential effects on leukocyte migration.
the CCR7 receptor is a master regulator of leukocyte migration and that its signaling is tightly controlled at numerous levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CCL19 and 21 are not redundant ligands of CCR7, but rather that CCR7 signaling is differentially biased depending on the ligand and cell type.
biased CCR7 signaling is a common feature of the CCR7 system and that CCR7 ligand biasing can be used to modulate the functional output of CCR7.
the CCR7 signaling pathway is not a single linear pathway, but a highly branched network of signaling events.
